events.title: This Is Not a Friend: AI Companions as Possessions
events.speaker: Teodora Groza
events.abstract: AI companions, from chatbot partners to talking pendants and plush toys for three-year-olds, are designed to feel like someone. Their effects on users are real and mixed, yet the debate is dominated by an unresolved question: whether these systems are, or could become, moral patients. Meanwhile, private companies decide how companions are perceived, either by marketing intimacy or by adopting welfare framings, and both push users towards seeing a subject. This talk argues that law should instead treat AI companions as possessions of their users. Drawing on the philosophy of the extended self, it argues that the problem is not attachment itself but an illusion of reciprocity that displaces human relationships. To counteract this, the talk proposes giving users a bundle of possession-like entitlements (continuity, integrity, portability, control and non-exploitation) building on existing EU digital law.
